AGENTS.md
# Baseline Platform Profiles

This repository maintains two technical foundations with one shared design system. The root application is the **EmDash Node.js + SQLite** foundation. Generated static projects use native Astro Content Collections and static output. All profiles use npm, Tailwind CSS v4, `src/styles/global.css`, token checks, layout primitives and `/_styleguide` calibration. Adapt the content model, visual language and this file for each real site.

## Platform Profile routing

| Profile ID | Editing | Hosting/runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `static` | Developer/agent edits typed Markdown files | Astro static build; no database or server adapter |
| `static-sveltia` | Sveltia SPA edits the same Git-owned files | Same static build; OAuth proxy or PAT for GitHub authentication |
| `emdash` | Relational CMS, Portable Text, live canvas and MCP | Node/SQLite/local media, or separately configured Workers/D1/R2 |

Read `baseline.config.json` in generated sites; absence in this root means the existing EmDash application. Profile is independent of Standard/Express track. Generate static sites with `npm run init:profile -- --profile static|static-sveltia --out <new-directory>`; do not prune a cloned CMS project in place. EmDash uses the existing full repository template. See `docs/platform-profiles.md`.

Static profiles use `new-site-workflow`, `site-art-direction`, `astro-site-design` and `impeccable`; skip EmDash setup, modeling, building, CLI and plugin specialists. Do not add CMS dependencies to satisfy an inapplicable check. Generated CI and `sync:baseline` use the installed profile's bounded inventory. Review staged updates before applying, preserve locally calibrated tokens, and verify afterward (`docs/baseline-updates.md`). EmDash-specific commands and rules below apply only to `emdash`.

`SiteShell.astro` is the shared document/landmark shell; platform `Base.astro` wrappers supply navigation and contributions. `ResponsiveImage.astro` is native Astro presentation; `EmDashImage.astro` alone resolves CMS storage. Common styleguide specimens run on both foundations, with EmDash extensions kept separate. Static routes use native `getStaticPaths()`/`render()` and the typed schema in `src/content.config.ts`. Sveltia's paired admin form must match that schema.

## First steps in a new site repository

1. Read `README.md`, inspect the installed tooling and existing files, and use the package manager matching the lockfile (`npm`).
2. Use `new-site-workflow` as the entry point when adapting this starter into a site or carrying out a full rebuild. Choose either the **Standard Track (7 Stages)** for complex migrations/multi-locale builds or the **Express Track (3 Checkpoints)** for smaller greenfield sites (`<= 6` routes, single locale), and load each specialist skill when its stage begins.
3. Keep site-specific facts in their established home: here by default, or in an explicitly adopted optional `PROJECT.md` linked here. Keep working rules and the `## Art Direction Record` in this file; link actual content models, route inventories, hosting and localization configuration rather than maintaining competing copies. Do not carry the starter's sample content or English text into a client site by default; use `npm run design:tokens -- --init-client --lane <lane>` when initializing a client site to seed tokens, write the record, and prune starter sample-page gate exceptions.
4. Only run `npm run sync:emdash-skills` or `npm run sync:site-skills -- --check` when explicitly checking for upstream skill updates or refreshing an older checkout (`docs/skill-synchronization.md`). On a fresh clone, use the checked-in skills under `.agents/skills/` directly without a blocking sync detour.


## Project records

`AGENTS.md` owns working rules and the compact Art Direction Record. Optional
`PROJECT.md` owns an adopted client brief, scope, ownership and nonvisual decision
rationale. The selected optional `DESIGN.md` owns visual references/interchange;
CSS and application configuration own implemented values. Current progress belongs
in the existing tracker or a short handoff when needed. Use one home per fact,
link the others, and resolve conflicts by subject and evidence rather than filename
precedence. Missing optional files do not block authorized work. See
`docs/project-context.md` and `PROJECT.example.md`.

## Where to work

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `astro.config.mjs` | Node adapter, EmDash SQLite/local-media setup, Tailwind v4 |
| `seed/seed.json` | Initial Posts/Pages schema and sample content; a seed is not a deploy-time content migration |
| `src/live.config.ts` | EmDash live collection registration |
| `src/styles/global.css` | Neutral `@theme` tokens, base rules, flow spacing `.flow`, `.content-grid`, and shared layout classes |
| `src/components/` | `Section`, `Container` (including `breakout`), `Grid`, `Card`, native `Disclosure`, wrapping `Cluster` and intrinsic `Sidebar` primitives (`docs/native-composition.md`) |
| `src/layouts/Base.astro` | Site shell, EmDash page contributions, menu, and widgets |
| `src/pages/` | Server-rendered public routes |
| `.agents/skills/` | Project-local EmDash and Vermeulen Solutions workflows |

## Skills and documentation

- `new-site-workflow`: required sequencing and handoffs for a complete new site or rebuild.
- `site-art-direction`: brief-led visual direction before frontend implementation. Consult `references/aesthetic-lanes.md` to select an aesthetic lane and define the narrative metaphor.
- `impeccable`: bounded visual critique and UI refinement after rendered pages are available.
- `building-emdash-site`: content queries, schema, Portable Text, site features.
- `emdash-cli`: current CLI operations and editing flow.
- `creating-plugins`: plugin implementation when a site actually needs one.
- `emdash-site-setup`: hosting and sandbox runner selection, deployment, and site transfer.
- `wordpress-to-emdash-content`: WordPress import, media, and form behavior.
- `astro-site-design`: visual inspection and maintainable public Astro presentation. For existing-site rebuilds, read its migration visual-audit reference before implementing pages.

For complete site work, the normal sequence is: brief and evidence → platform decisions → content and routes → art direction → representative Astro/EmDash implementation → Impeccable visual critique and refinement → full review and delivery. A scoped task may begin at the earliest affected stage, but must check whether its inputs are already established and update downstream decisions when they are invalidated.

During new-site design setup, explain **layout spacing**. Express defaults to shared responsive spacing and brief-led density (balanced when unspecified), without a separate CSS-policy question. Standard asks about shared versus custom spacing only when it is a material unresolved decision. Use `new-site-workflow`'s persona-informed discovery questions and defaults, reuse prior answers and continue authorized work without mandatory checkpoint stops. Record visual density, exceptions and approved/assumed direction with the Art Direction Record here; keep nonvisual decisions and content/maintenance ownership in the established context home. No settings panel or external-product terminology is needed.

For WordPress migrations, classify repeated material that is not a registered custom post type before implementing routes. Keep a substantial content-candidate register in `audit/content-candidate-register.md` and link it here; classify each candidate as a collection, page content, site setting, plugin/integration data, or deliberate exclusion.

Use the live [EmDash docs](https://docs.emdashcms.com/) or configured docs MCP to verify APIs and commands. The three EmDash-authored skills are upstream mirrors; change custom guidance in the other skill directories, not in those mirrors.

## Implementation rules

- Before site-specific visual implementation anywhere under `src/` or `public/`, save one complete `## Art Direction Record` in this file with Aesthetic Lane, Narrative Metaphor, Typography Pairing, Token Physics (Canvas, Action/Accent, Borders, Spatial Density), and 2–3 Site Anti-Patterns separated by semicolons. “Save” means write to disk; a Git commit is not required or implied. Run `npm run check:art-direction -- --require-record` before implementing. Route inventory and content modeling may precede this gate; visual route templates may not.
- The gate applies to site visual work regardless of file extension or directory relocation. Functional fixes that preserve the visual system, backend/platform setup, starter infrastructure maintenance, and isolated concept studies under `audit/visual-concepts/` are scoped exceptions. Document source-file exceptions in `audit/design-gate-exceptions.json` with an exact path, concrete reason, and SHA-256 of UTF-8 content normalized to LF; an edit invalidates its exception. Never exempt a directory or client page implementation. Exception changes require the same review as code changes.
- `npm run check:art-direction` checks changed visual source against HEAD (or `--base <revision>`) and validates the record unless exact infrastructure exceptions cover it. CI runs this check. This is structural outcome validation, not prevention of writes, proof of decision chronology, human approval, or design quality. True pre-write enforcement requires a guard in the agent tool runner. Keep evidence and approved versus assumed decisions explicit; revisit the record when the brief changes.
- The reusable starter intentionally has no invented client Art Direction Record. When adapting it to a client site, create the real record and retain only applicable exceptions.
- Use `npm run design:tokens` (`scripts/design-system.mjs`) for agent-first token calibration and validation. Seed a canonical Aesthetic Lane preset, `## Art Direction Record`, and Stage 4.5 calibration table (`npm run design:tokens -- --lane <lane> --write --write-record --write-calibration` or `--seed-accent <color> --type-scale <ratio>`), refine brand tokens in `src/styles/global.css`, and run `npm run design:tokens` + `npm run test:design` to verify WCAG AA perceptual contrast across default and `[data-surface="dark"]` contexts, fluid `clamp()` bounds, custom font loading, EmDash `.edit.` proxy bindings, and `/_styleguide` specimen coverage. Apply `[data-hero-asset]` to media itself.
- Keep CMS routes server-rendered. Use EmDash's content and media APIs rather than assuming database table shapes or string image fields. When a site requires drag-and-drop visual landing pages or popups, evaluate the optional native EmVB plugin (`@perkyzz/emvb` + `@perkyzz/emvb-mcp`) during Stage 2 and pass `canvasStyles` so the visual builder inherits `src/styles/global.css`.
- When Astro route caching is enabled, register cache hints for every EmDash query used to render a route, including shared settings and menus. Check the installed EmDash version for the current `*WithCacheHint` helpers.
- All authored CSS lives in `@layer base` or `@layer components`; contextual defaults use zero-specificity `:where()` selectors so `@layer utilities` overrides them without `!important`. Never leave normal selector rules outside a named layer. Component `<style>` blocks follow the same contract; keyframes stay outside the layer.
- Site-owned Base explicitly selects `SiteShell spacingPolicy="automatic-v2"`; the shared shell defaults to legacy for installed-site compatibility. Under v2, Section owns block padding and a container stack gap, ordinary Container owns a content stack gap, Grid owns its grid gap, and `.site-main` owns horizontal gutters once without inferring block rhythm. `spacing="none"` removes padding only; nested primitive defaults reset independently. Use `layout="custom"` when the caller owns display/gap. Breakout retains its named grid. Keep local `--section-padding`, `--container-gap`, `--grid-gap` separate from inherited root-context aliases `--layout-section-padding`, `--layout-container-gap`, `--layout-content-gap`, `--layout-grid-gap`. These regular aliases reuse existing scales; do not add another `@theme` scale.
- Render editorial Portable Text through `RichText`, which establishes `.flow` and `data-editorial-content`. Generic `.flow` only spaces visible direct siblings; handwritten prose needs the editorial marker. Composite internals are bounded by `data-editorial-island`; nested editorial bodies own their controls. `flow={false}` relinquishes rhythm and prose defaults (wrapperless unless attributes require a plain wrapper). `.article-body` is a margin wrapper. Do not combine flow/space-y child margins and a layout gap for the same relationship. Verify actual CMS typing/save/reload when changing renderer/edit targets; attributes alone are not proof.
- Use the existing neutral tokens and structural components as a starting API; derive brand values from the site's actual brief and visual evidence. Keep repeated content types in collections and reusable Astro templates when editors need to add entries.
- Treat WordPress imports, public page design, and deployed site transfer as distinct operations. A code deployment does not copy local CMS content to a remote database.
- For multilingual sites, use EmDash's native row-per-locale model linked by translation groups. Never create duplicate language fields (e.g. title_en, content_en) on a single collection row. Set prefixDefaultLocale: false in astro.config.mjs to keep the EmDash admin functional. See docs/internationalization.md.

## Starter standards and optional design interchange

- **Stage 4.5 component calibration:** After saving the art direction and before broad page assembly, calibrate primitives on `/_styleguide` and record evidence in `audit/component-calibration.md` (`npm run design:tokens -- --write-calibration`). Follow `.agents/skills/astro-site-design/references/component-quarantine.md` for open structural slots, semantic composites, and surface-aware actions.
- **Asset provenance & native image delivery:** Download site content imagery to `src/assets/` or the EmDash Media Library — never directly to `public/`. Document unchanged-URL passthrough exceptions (favicons, `robots.txt`, fonts) and prefer Astro `<Image>` / `<Picture>` / `getImage()` with EmDash's storage-backed media endpoint (`docs/image-delivery.md`).
- **Partner & gallery primitives:** Compose `Card`, `PartnersPanel`, `LogoTicker`, `ResponsiveImage`, `EditorialImage`, `PhotoGallery`, `RichText`, and bounded form recovery (`docs/reusable-public-patterns.md`). `LogoTicker` accepts only trusted, noninteractive, ID-free list items without scripts, islands, or edit proxies; linked/editor-owned partners use an unduplicated list.
- **Certified baseline & registry:** Scoped certified baseline is Astro `7.4.0` / EmDash `1.3.0` on Node `22.22.2+` or `24.15+` (Node 24 LTS recommended; see `standards/manifest.json` and `docs/starter-meta-review.md`). Current development tooling requires Node `^22.22.3 || ^24.16.0 || >=26.3.0`; the older scoped certification is historical evidence, not a claim that the new lint tool runs below this floor. `docs/design-interchange.md` defines the optional `DESIGN.md` bridge; `AGENTS.md` and `src/styles/global.css` retain authority. Complete new sites with `npm run site:register` (`docs/site-registry.md`).
- **Framework docs MCP & local visual regression:** Consult Astro Docs MCP and EmDash Docs MCP against installed versions (`docs/agent-documentation.md`). Run `npm run test:visual` locally on Windows only (`docs/visual-regression.md`); never run visual regression in automated CI or production builds.

## Day-2 client changes and maintenance

When modifying an existing, deployed site in response to client change requests, preserve the token and primitive hierarchy:

- **Global visual changes** (radii, brand colors, typography, fluid spacing): update existing `@theme` scales for a deliberate whole-site change. For structural spacing relationships use regular `:root --layout-*` aliases; for a regional request use a layered contextual alias, then a primitive gap prop or utility for a single instance. Preview `npm run design:tokens -- --set "--root:--layout-grid-gap=calc(var(--spacing-grid) * 0.75)" --json`; add `--write` only after reviewing the candidate, or `--write --write-calibration` for saved-source evidence. CSS is the sole configuration store; no spacing admin panel is needed. Run token checks and rendered acceptance; align the client's Art Direction Record if core physics shift. See `docs/design-framework.md` for scope recipes and bounded expression support.
- **Component styling and variants** (cards, media frames, buttons, tickers): modify primitives in `src/components/` (e.g. `Card.astro`, `Grid.astro`) rather than scattering one-off overrides in page templates. Verify styleguide specimens via `npm run test:design` or on `/_styleguide`.
- **Layout and section refactoring** (e.g., converting a grid into a bento or timeline): compose using existing layout primitives (`<Section>`, `<Container>`, `<Grid>`) and semantic CSS referencing existing tokens (`--spacing-grid`, `--radius-card`). Do not introduce arbitrary pixel values or breakpoint soup.
- **New pages and section additions**: Distinguish editor-managed content (add entries to existing CMS collections or Markdown content) from structural routes (create in `src/pages/`). For new routes and sections, wrap in `Base.astro`, compose with layout primitives (`<Section>`, `<Container>`, `<Grid>`), vary section pacing and background surfaces to avoid repetitive stacking, and bind CMS edit proxies (`{...entry.edit.*}`) when EmDash-backed.
- **Navigation & menu sync**: When adding, renaming, or removing routes, update site navigation links in `Base.astro`, shared navigation configs, or EmDash CMS menus and `seed/seed.json`.
- **Asset placement**: Place new photographic or vector assets in `src/assets/` using `<ResponsiveImage>` or native Astro `<Image>`, or upload them into the EmDash Media Library. Never place site content imagery directly into `public/`.
- **Renaming or removing routes**: Always preserve SEO and existing links by adding 301 redirects (via `redirects` in `astro.config.mjs` for static sites or EmDash redirect middleware for CMS sites).
- **Verification:** Always run `npm run verify` (lint, art direction, token audits, typecheck, tests) before submitting changes.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev
npm run verify
npm test
npm run check:art-direction
npm run design:tokens
npm run test:design
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm run sync:emdash-skills
npm run sync:site-skills
```

Use the local URL printed by Astro for `/_emdash/admin`; the port may differ from 4321.


## Engineering verification loop

For the EmDash foundation, preflight with `npm.cmd run doctor`, use
`npm.cmd run verify:fast` during edits, then run `npm.cmd run verify`,
`npm.cmd run build`, and `npm.cmd run audit:html` against that fresh build
before handoff. On Unix use `npm` in place of `npm.cmd`. Set up the local
Git pre-commit hook once with `npm.cmd run setup:hooks`; it runs doctor and
verify:fast and preserves existing hook managers. It supplements the final gate
and CI; Git hooks are local and can be bypassed. The HTML audit checks emitted
HTML or automatically captures linked public SSR responses from the local
production CMS. Missing published content or broken navigation fails the audit;
see `docs/html-integrity.md` for capture limits and snapshot inspection. For generated
static profiles, inspect the installed package scripts and use their verification
commands; do not add CMS tooling to satisfy an unavailable command.

## Production runtime hardening

- CMS/raw/plugin/nested flags use `src/lib/cms-flag.ts`: `isCmsFlagSet` accepts true/1; `isCmsFlagEnabled` defaults nullish optional opt-outs on and otherwise requires true/1. Avoid strict true checks or general truthiness at these boundaries. Declared loader booleans are normalized in EmDash 1.3; arbitrary nested/plugin/raw values are not. Malformed strings fail closed.
- Follow `docs/cloudflare-backup-restore.md` before production mutations: record a D1 recovery bookmark (plan-specific retention), media snapshot and full encryption-key escrow receipt. `site export --output file.emdash` transfers content into an empty target; it is not DR. Never reset production to fix authentication/imports.
- Follow `docs/edge-cache-lifecycle.md` for explicit HTML TTLs, no HTML SWR, client toolbar, seven-day immutable asset carry-forward, URL exclusions and real publish/purge/scheduler checks. URL normalization is opt-in after checking public slugs. Keep Node/SQLite and static profiles independent from Cloudflare.
- Follow `docs/newsletter-architecture.md` for POST-only consent, scanner-safe GET/HEAD, signature-first exact domain isolation, known-subscriber-only updates and idempotency. Preserve optional providers/plugins until site acceptance.
- Starter functional/metadata changes preserve visual tokens and presentation; exact LF hash exceptions in `audit/design-gate-exceptions.json` document infrastructure scope. No client art direction is invented for this hardening.

# EmDash CLI

The EmDash CLI (`emdash`, with the short alias `em`) manages EmDash CMS instances. Commands fall into two categories:

- **Local commands** work with project files or a configured database: `init`, `doctor`, `seed`, `migrate`, `export-seed`, and `secrets`.
- **Remote commands** talk to a running EmDash instance: `types`, `login`, `logout`, `whoami`, `content`, `schema`, `media`, `search`, `taxonomy`, `menu`, and `site`.

Run `npx emdash --help` and `npx emdash <command> --help` for the installed version's exact commands and flags. Resolve the current target with a read command before a destructive or bulk mutation; examples in this skill do not authorize changing an instance the user did not place in scope.

## Authentication

Remote commands resolve auth automatically:

1. `--token` flag
2. `EMDASH_TOKEN` env var
3. Stored credentials from `emdash login`
4. Dev bypass (localhost only — no token needed)

For a localhost development server with the development bypass enabled, the client can authenticate automatically. For a remote instance, run `emdash login --url https://example.com` or provide a scoped token.

## Custom Headers & Reverse Proxies

Sites behind Cloudflare Access or other reverse proxies need auth headers on every request. The CLI supports this via `--header` flags and environment variables.

### Service tokens for automation

```bash
# Provide sensitive headers through the environment in CI.
export EMDASH_HEADERS="CF-Access-Client-Id: xxx
CF-Access-Client-Secret: yyy"
npx emdash whoami --url https://example.com
```

`emdash login --header` persists custom headers to `~/.config/emdash/auth.json` for later commands. Prefer environment-provided headers in CI so a service secret is not written to the credential file or shell history.

### Cloudflare Access Browser Flow

If you don't have service tokens and `cloudflared` is installed, the CLI will automatically:

1. Detect when Access blocks the request
2. Try to get a cached JWT via `cloudflared access token`
3. Fall back to `cloudflared access login` for browser-based auth

This works for interactive use but isn't suitable for CI. Use service tokens for automation.

### Generic Reverse Proxy Auth

The `--header` flag works with any auth scheme:

```bash
# Basic auth
npx emdash login --url https://example.com -H "Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz"

# Custom auth header
npx emdash login --url https://example.com -H "X-API-Key: secret123"
```

## Quick Reference

### Database Setup

For normal site startup, use the project's package script. The first request runs pending migrations and, before setup is completed, applies the bundled seed's schema and structure once; sample content comes from the setup wizard, `/_emdash/api/setup/dev-bypass`, or `emdash seed`. The Astro integration generates `emdash-env.d.ts` when the server starts.

```bash
# Start the site with its package script
pnpm dev

# Export an existing database as a seed file
# (the runtime auto-discovers .emdash/seed.json on first boot;
# `mkdir -p` because the directory may not exist yet)
mkdir -p .emdash
npx emdash export-seed > .emdash/seed.json
npx emdash export-seed --with-content=all > .emdash/seed.json
```

### Type Generation

```bash
# Generate types from local dev server
npx emdash types

# Generate from remote
npx emdash types --url https://example.com

# Custom output path
npx emdash types --output src/types/cms.ts
```

Writes `.emdash/types.ts` (TypeScript interfaces) and `.emdash/schema.json`.

### Authentication

```bash
# Login (OAuth Device Flow)
npx emdash login --url https://example.com

# Check current user
npx emdash whoami

# Logout
npx emdash logout

# Generate an encryption key for deployment
npx emdash secrets generate
```

### Content CRUD

The CLI is designed for agents. Create and update auto-publish by default so agents get read-after-write consistency without managing drafts.

```bash
# List content
npx emdash content list posts
npx emdash content list posts --status published --limit 10

# Get a single item (Portable Text fields converted to markdown)
# Returns draft data if a pending draft exists
npx emdash content get posts 01ABC123
npx emdash content get posts 01ABC123 --raw        # skip PT->markdown conversion
npx emdash content get posts 01ABC123 --published   # ignore pending drafts

# Create content (auto-publishes by default)
npx emdash content create posts --data '{"title": "Hello", "body": "# World"}'
npx emdash content create posts --file post.json --slug hello-world
npx emdash content create posts --draft --data '...'  # keep as draft
cat post.json | npx emdash content create posts --stdin

# Update (requires --rev from a prior get, auto-publishes by default)
npx emdash content update posts 01ABC123 --rev MToyMDI2... --data '{"title": "Updated"}'
npx emdash content update posts 01ABC123 --rev MToyMDI2... --draft --data '...'  # keep as draft

# Delete (soft delete)
npx emdash content delete posts 01ABC123

# Lifecycle
npx emdash content publish posts 01ABC123
npx emdash content unpublish posts 01ABC123
npx emdash content schedule posts 01ABC123 --at 2026-03-01T09:00:00Z
npx emdash content restore posts 01ABC123
```

### Schema Management

```bash
# List collections
npx emdash schema list

# Get collection with fields
npx emdash schema get posts

# Create collection
npx emdash schema create articles --label Articles --description "Blog articles"

# Delete a collection after inspecting it and confirming the target
npx emdash schema get articles
npx emdash schema delete articles

# Add field
npx emdash schema add-field posts body --type portableText --label "Body Content"
npx emdash schema add-field posts featured --type boolean --required

# Remove field
npx emdash schema remove-field posts featured
```

`schema add-field` supports the field types printed by `npx emdash schema add-field --help`. The full product schema supports additional field types that are not necessarily creatable through this command.

### Media

```bash
# List media
npx emdash media list
npx emdash media list --mime image/png

# Upload
npx emdash media upload ./photo.jpg --alt "A sunset" --caption "Bristol, 2026"

# Get / delete
npx emdash media get 01MEDIA123
npx emdash media delete 01MEDIA123
```

### Search

```bash
npx emdash search "hello world"
npx emdash search "hello" --collection posts --limit 5
```

### Taxonomies

```bash
npx emdash taxonomy list
npx emdash taxonomy terms categories
npx emdash taxonomy add-term categories --name "Tech" --slug tech
```

### Site Export and Import

`emdash site` copies a whole site (content model, content, history, settings, and media, but no users or secrets) into a `.emdash` site package, and imports a package into an empty site. The token needs `admin`, which the `emdash login` token has, or the `transfer:export`, `transfer:analyze`, and `transfer:execute` scopes. An `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` error means the token has neither. A package holds every entry and the email addresses of authors and commenters: treat it like a database backup.

```bash
# Export (re-run the same command to resume after an interruption)
npx emdash site export --url https://old.example.com --output site.emdash
npx emdash site export --url https://old.example.com --output site.emdash --no-comments

# Import, step 1: upload and analyze; prints the plan and its digest
npx emdash site import site.emdash --url https://new.example.com --analyze
npx emdash site import site.emdash --url https://new.example.com --analyze \
  --map-principal editor@example.com=editor@example.com --use-target-title

# Import, step 2: execute exactly the reviewed plan
npx emdash site import site.emdash --url https://new.example.com --plan sha256:<hex> --confirm

# Follow up on an import by operation id
npx emdash site import status <operation-id> --url https://new.example.com
npx emdash site import resume <operation-id> [site.emdash] --url https://new.example.com
npx emdash site import receipt <operation-id> --url https://new.example.com

# Stop an import, or lift the write block a failed or cancelled import leaves
# (neither deletes what the import wrote; --yes skips the prompt)
npx emdash site import cancel <operation-id> --url https://new.example.com
npx emdash site import abandon <operation-id> --url https://new.example.com
```

Show the user the plan (differences from the source site, warnings, blockers, principal mappings) and get their confirmation before running `--confirm`; it writes to the target site and blocks other writes there until it finishes. `site import` exits `2` when the plan has blockers, and `site import status` exits `1` for an import that failed, was cancelled or abandoned, or expired. Only cancel or abandon an import when the user asks: abandoning leaves partial data on the site, which then has to be reset before another import. `--map-principal` takes `<principal id or email>=<user id, email, or none>` and is repeatable; decision flags only work with `--analyze`, and each change produces a new plan digest. The public site is not hidden during an import, so the target should stay private until the command prints a receipt with `receiptDigestValid: true`.

## Drafts and Publishing

The CLI auto-publishes on `create` and `update` by default. This means:

- **`create`** creates the item and immediately publishes it
- **`update`** updates the item and publishes if a draft revision was created
- **`get`** returns draft data if a pending draft exists (e.g. from the admin UI)

Use `--draft` on create/update to skip auto-publishing. Use `--published` on get to ignore pending drafts.

Collections that support revisions store edits as draft revisions. The CLI handles this transparently — agents don't need to know whether a collection uses revisions or not.

## JSON Output

All remote commands support `--json` for machine-readable output. It's auto-enabled when stdout is piped. `emdash site` always writes progress to stderr, so stdout holds only the JSON result; errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`.

```bash
# Pipe to jq
npx emdash content list posts --json | jq '.items[].slug'

# Use in scripts
ID=$(npx emdash content create posts --data '{"title":"Hello"}' --json | jq -r '.id')
```

# AI Agent & Harness Configuration

Baseline keeps repository instructions, skills and npm commands independent of a particular agent harness. Instruction discovery, skill discovery and MCP configuration still depend on the tool and version you use.

Whether you use Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Windsurf, Antigravity, OMP, Hermes, Aider or another assistant, the maintained project sources are:

1. **Repository Instructions (`AGENTS.md`):** Repository rules, architectural boundaries and verification standards. Ask your assistant to read this file if its harness does not load it automatically.
2. **Project Skills (`.agents/skills/`):** `SKILL.md` files and references covering site discovery, art direction, component quarantine and CMS modeling. Use native skill discovery where supported; otherwise explicitly read the applicable skill and its relevant references.
3. **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** Open JSON-RPC standard for live framework documentation, community `DESIGN.md` systems, UI component sourcing, visual prototyping, and site content management (see [`.mcp.example.json`](../.mcp.example.json)).
4. **Deterministic Shell Tooling:** Standard npm commands (`npm run ...`) runnable in any bash, PowerShell, or automated execution environment.

For optional installed-project discovery, use `npm run baseline:inspect -- --json`
after installing dependencies. It reports source-derived facts and paths without
executing project configuration. See [scope and limits](project-inspection.md);
it does not replace repository instructions, skills or verification.

## 1. Connecting Official Documentation via MCP

Allow your coding assistant to consult live, up-to-date Astro and EmDash documentation without hallucinating deprecated APIs. 

### Claude Code and Cursor:

The root [`.mcp.example.json`](../.mcp.example.json) contains only the two public documentation servers. Generated static projects include only Astro documentation; they do not need EmDash tools. For Claude Code, merge the entries into project `.mcp.json`. For Cursor, merge them into `.cursor/mcp.json`. Preserve existing settings; do not overwrite a configured file. Other clients may require a different schema, as shown below.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "astro-docs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp"
    },
    "emdash-docs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://docs.emdashcms.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### OpenAI Codex Configuration:
Merge project connections into `.codex/config.toml` (project configuration must be trusted by Codex):

```toml
[mcp_servers.astro-docs]
url = "https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp"

[mcp_servers.emdash-docs]
url = "https://docs.emdashcms.com/mcp"
```

### OpenCode Configuration:

Merge these entries into `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc`. Its `mcp` object and `remote` transport value differ from the `mcpServers` / `http` example:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "astro-docs": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp"
    },
    "emdash-docs": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://docs.emdashcms.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Omit `emdash-docs` for static profiles. In every client, inspect its MCP server/tool list and make a documentation search to verify the actual connection. In Codex, `codex mcp list` shows registered servers; a successful tool call verifies availability.

On the root EmDash foundation, this additional command probes the public documentation servers directly:

```sh
npm run check:docs-mcp
```

It does not load or validate your agent's configuration and cannot establish that your client has registered either server. Generated static projects do not include this command. On Windows PowerShell use `npm.cmd` / `npx.cmd` for npm examples in this guide.

## 3. Site-Level EmDash CMS MCP Setup

Connect your MCP client's supported OAuth flow to `/_emdash/api/mcp`, sign in as
the intended existing account and keep only the scopes needed for its task.
EmDash checks both scopes and the account's role. Personal access tokens can also
be created and revoked in **Admin → Users → API tokens**. Use these supported
interfaces for hosted sites and D1. See the [MCP authentication and scope contract](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/).

For a local Node/SQLite instance, the compatibility helper below supports explicit
account selection, a read-only plan, finite expiry and owner-bound revocation.
It still accesses EmDash 1.3's token table directly: PAT creation is an admin UI
route rather than a supported public REST operation in this version. Do not use
this fallback to mutate production databases; follow the runtime's recovery
procedure before any authorized production mutation.

```bash
# Help only; does not open or create a database:
npm run mcp:token -- --help
# Inspect the proposed read-only grants for an existing account:
npm run mcp:token -- --db data.db --user editor@example.test --preset read-only --url http://localhost:4321
# Create only after reviewing that plan; use the actual origin printed by Astro:
npm run mcp:token -- --db data.db --user editor@example.test --preset read-only --url http://localhost:4321 --apply
# Plan revocation, then repeat with --apply to revoke exactly this owner's token:
npm run mcp:token -- --db data.db --user editor@example.test --revoke TOKEN_ID
```

| Preset | Grants | Minimum existing role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read-only` (default) | Content, media, schema and settings reads | Editor |
| `content-authoring` | Content and media reads/writes | Contributor |
| `setup` | Core content/media/schema/settings writes, taxonomy and menu management | Admin |

Presets never grant `admin`, plugin-tool or site-transfer scopes. `setup` is
explicit elevated access. For narrower or advanced grants, use `--scopes` with
an exact comma-separated list instead of `--preset`; invalid scopes and grants
beyond the chosen account's role are rejected rather than silently expanded or
clamped. For example, a Subscriber can hold `--scopes content:read,media:read`.
In EmDash 1.3, `content:write` also grants taxonomy/menu writes for compatibility;
publication, owned-content limits and draft visibility still follow the account
role. A read-only token for an administrator may therefore read drafts.

Draft read access is also broader than edit ownership: a Contributor can read
another user's draft while being unable to edit it or publish their own draft.
The authoring preset therefore does not isolate private drafts by owner. Use a
Subscriber with the narrower read scopes above when access should cover only
published content. These boundaries were exercised through live MCP in the
[local role acceptance](../audit/autonomous-evaluation-2026-10-21/roles.md).

No account is selected or created automatically. `--db` must name an existing,
non-linked local file; `--user` must resolve to one existing account. Without
`--apply`, the helper opens the database read-only and returns a JSON plan with
no secret. Creation returns the token once in JSON, its ID, owner, exact grants
and expiry; only its hash is stored in the database. Expiry defaults to 30 days;
override it with `--expires-at <future-ISO-timestamp>`. Keep the token in private
client settings using the client schema above; do not commit the creation output.
The legacy `--d1` SQL path is removed. Static profiles have no EmDash MCP endpoint.

# Editing Flow

How content editing works through the CLI. Covers Portable Text conversion, `_rev` tokens, and raw mode.

## Portable Text and Markdown

EmDash stores rich text as [Portable Text](https://portabletext.org/) (PT) — a structured JSON format. The CLI automatically converts between PT and markdown so you work with a familiar text format.

### Automatic Conversion

- **On read**: PT arrays in `portableText` fields are converted to markdown strings
- **On write**: markdown strings in `portableText` fields are converted back to PT arrays
- **Non-PT fields** (string, text, number, etc.) pass through unchanged

The CLI detects which fields need conversion by fetching the collection's field schema.

### Supported Markdown Syntax

Standard blocks (lossless round-trip):

| Markdown                     | PT block                                   |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `# Heading` through `######` | h1-h6 blocks                               |
| Plain paragraph              | normal block                               |
| `> Quote`                    | blockquote                                 |
| `- item` / `* item`          | bullet list (nesting via 2-space indent)   |
| `1. item`                    | numbered list (nesting via 2-space indent) |
| ` ``` ```lang``` `           | code block with language                   |
| `![alt](url)`                | image block                                |

Inline marks:

| Markdown      | PT mark         |
| ------------- | --------------- |
| `**bold**`    | `strong`        |
| `_italic_`    | `em`            |
| `` `code` ``  | `code`          |
| `~~strike~~`  | `strikethrough` |
| `[text](url)` | link annotation |

### Unknown Blocks (Opaque Fences)

Blocks the converter doesn't recognize (custom blocks, embeds, etc.) are serialized as HTML comments:

```markdown
<!--ec:block {"_type":"callout","level":"warning","text":"Be careful"} -->
```

These survive round-trips intact. You can see and move them, but editing the JSON risks corruption. On write, they're deserialized back to the original PT block.

### Raw Mode

Skip markdown conversion entirely to work with raw PT JSON:

```bash
npx emdash content get posts 01ABC123 --raw
```

Use raw mode when:

- You need exact control over PT structure
- You're working with custom block types
- You're copying PT between items without transformation

### Writing Content

When creating or updating content, each field is checked:

- `portableText` field + **string value** → converts markdown to PT before sending
- `portableText` field + **array value** → sends as raw PT (no conversion)
- Any other field type → sends as-is

```bash
# Markdown string — converted to PT automatically
npx emdash content create posts --data '{"title": "Hello", "body": "# Welcome\n\nThis is **bold**."}'

# Raw PT array — passed through as-is
npx emdash content create posts --data '{"title": "Hello", "body": [{"_type": "block", "children": [{"_type": "span", "text": "Welcome"}]}]}'
```

## Auto-Publishing

The CLI is designed for agents. It auto-publishes on `create` and `update` by default so agents get read-after-write consistency without managing the draft/publish lifecycle.

### How It Works

- **`create`** — creates the item, then publishes it. The returned item is in `published` status.
- **`update`** — updates the item. If the collection uses revisions and the update created a draft revision, it auto-publishes to promote the draft to the content table. The returned item reflects the updated data.
- **`get`** — returns the latest state. If a pending draft exists (e.g. someone edited in the admin UI but didn't publish), the draft data is returned instead of the published data. Use `--published` to see only published data.

Use `--draft` on create/update to skip auto-publishing.

### Why Auto-Publish?

EmDash collections can support draft revisions. When they do, `update` writes data to a draft revision instead of the content table. Without auto-publish, an agent would update, then `get` the item, and see stale published data — not the changes it just made. Auto-publish eliminates this confusion.

## Read-Before-Write

Updates use `_rev` tokens for optimistic concurrency — the same principle as a file editing tool that requires you to read a file before you can edit it. You must see what you're overwriting.

### The Analogy

Think of it like a filesystem edit tool:

1. You **read** the file to see its current contents
2. You decide what to change
3. You **write** with a reference to the version you read

If someone else changed the file between your read and your write, the write fails — you can't overwrite changes you haven't seen. The `_rev` token is your proof that you've seen the current state.

### How It Works

1. `content get` returns the item with a `_rev` token in the output
2. You pass that `_rev` back to `content update` via `--rev`
3. The server checks: if the item has changed since your read, it returns **409 Conflict**
4. A successful update returns a new `_rev` for subsequent edits

### What Is a `_rev` Token?

An opaque base64 string. Don't parse it — just pass it back.

### CLI Workflow

The CLI **requires** `--rev` on updates. The typical workflow:

```bash
# 1. Read the item — note the _rev in the output
npx emdash content get posts 01ABC123
# Output includes: _rev: MToyMDI2LTAyLTE0...

# 2. Update with the _rev you received — auto-publishes by default
npx emdash content update posts 01ABC123 \
  --rev MToyMDI2LTAyLTE0... \
  --data '{"title": "New Title"}'
# Output shows updated item with new _rev
```

If you try to update without `--rev`, the CLI rejects the command. This ensures you always know what you're overwriting.

### Conflict Handling

If someone else updated the item between your read and write, the CLI exits with code 1 and prints:

```text
 ERROR  Content has been modified since last read (version conflict)
```

Re-read with `get`, inspect the new state, then `update` with the fresh `_rev`.

### Locked Entries

A 409 does not always mean the item changed. If someone has the entry open in the admin, the CLI exits with code 1 and prints the lock holder's name:

```text
 ERROR  Ada is holding this entry
```

The CLI prints only the error message, not the HTTP status or error code. REST API consumers can distinguish this refusal by its `ENTRY_LOCKED` code. Re-reading does not clear it: the item has not changed, so a fresh `_rev` produces the same refusal. Either wait, or pass `--override-lock` to write anyway. An editor releases the lock when they close the entry, and a lock left behind by a crashed tab lapses seven minutes after their last heartbeat.

Overriding does not take the lock. The editor keeps it and their next save is rejected as a version conflict, so wait unless you know they have gone.

`--override-lock` is accepted by `content update`, `content delete`, `content publish`, `content unpublish` and `content schedule`. Collections with edit locking switched off never return `ENTRY_LOCKED`.

### Which Operations Need `_rev`?

Only `update`. All other operations are either idempotent or non-destructive:

| Command             | `--rev` needed? | Why                      |
| ------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------ |
| `content create`    | No              | Nothing exists yet       |
| `content update`    | **Yes**         | Overwrites existing data |
| `content delete`    | No              | Soft delete, reversible  |
| `content publish`   | No              | Idempotent status change |
| `content unpublish` | No              | Idempotent status change |
| `content schedule`  | No              | Only changes metadata    |
| `content restore`   | No              | Restores from trash      |

# Production HTML integrity

Run `npm.cmd run build`, then `npm.cmd run audit:html` (use `npm` on Unix).
The audit always checks the release artifact for leaked fixtures. Emitted HTML
is audited offline. When no HTML is emitted and `dist/server/entry.mjs` exists,
it reserves an available port in 49152–65535, starts that production entrypoint
on loopback with that `PORT`, captures public
HTML, stops the server in `finally`, and audits the snapshots.

The SSR runner uses the existing local CMS and loads its ignored `.env` using
Node's built-in env-file support. It makes anonymous GET requests; it does not
seed content, create an admin, sign in or bypass setup. Populate the local CMS
with representative published content before expecting a passing content audit.
A stale navigation link to an unpublished `/about` page is a real failure.

Capture starts at `/`, follows internal anchors' destinations (including queries
and local redirects), and requests a unique nonexistent route to verify a rendered
404 response. At least one linked successful sample page/post must be present;
an empty homepage alone cannot pass. A post listing is a page, not evidence of
individual article coverage: publish and link a sample post to exercise it.
Links to the page's canonical origin are fetched through loopback; external
destinations are never fetched. External redirects and CMS setup/auth redirects
fail capture rather than substituting an unrelated page.

The default capture deadline is 3.5 seconds, with forced shutdown after a 250ms
grace period. Capture is bounded to 64 response URLs and 2 MB per HTML response.
Deadline/limit failures exit nonzero and keep partial diagnostics. This is a
representative public crawl, not authentication, browser, or whole-site coverage.

Local HTTP/browser harnesses share `scripts/loopback-port.mjs`. They bind only
127.0.0.1 and use the dynamic/private port range to avoid Fetch/browser-blocked
ports, including on Windows machines where `PORT=0` can return a lower number.
Occupied or excluded ports are retried a bounded number of times. A child
process must bind after reservation release, so a cross-process race remains
possible and must fail readiness clearly. Performance deadlines are unchanged.

The root `npm test` runs the exhaustive tier inventory: unit files with concurrency
2, then rehearsal files with concurrency 1. `verify:fast` and fast CI use the same
unit cap. This separates bounded HTML performance checks from framework builds,
installs and heavy Git subprocesses rather than increasing their time budgets.

Each run writes a unique ignored `.emdash/snapshots/capture-*` directory. HTML
and `.ssr-snapshot.json` preserve original URL paths, queries, HTTP status and
redirect mappings so missing pages cannot pass merely because their error HTML
was saved. Same-page fragments on the 404 response still receive anchor checks.

To capture separately, run `node scripts/snapshot-ssr.mjs [dist]`. To repeat the
offline audit, run `node scripts/audit-html-integrity.mjs <capture-directory>`.
Snapshots are retained for inspection and may be removed when no longer needed.
On Ctrl+C or capture errors the runner stops its child and removes its signal
listeners. No external package is used by the capture or HTML audit scripts.

# EmDash 1.3 adoption and verification

This guide applies to the `emdash` Platform Profile. Static and Sveltia sites do
not acquire EmDash settings, admin callbacks, permissions or database adapters.
The release reference is [EmDash 1.3.0](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/releases/tag/emdash%401.3.0);
consult the installed package as well as current documentation when adapting code.

## Native AI-training opt-out

Settings → SEO exposes **Disallow AI training**, off by default. Its API/MCP value
is `seo.disallowAiTraining`; choose the policy with the site owner and save it using
the native settings UI, settings API or `settings_update` MCP tool. Preserve other
SEO settings when updating this property.

When enabled, EmDash's `/robots.txt` appends named training-crawler exclusions and
`Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no` to its default or custom robots content.
Existing search rules remain authoritative. Inspect the actual response after
saving, including any CDN cache or custom robots file/route that could shadow it.
The directives are voluntary crawler requests, not access control or a guarantee
that training stops.

Do not add a parallel `tdm-reservation` header or hardcoded training-crawler list
to `Base.astro`/`SiteShell.astro` to enable this feature. The native robots route
owns it. Baseline retains the upstream opt-in default. Static sites manage their
own intentional robots policy independently.

## Roles and external authentication

| Value | Role | Relevant authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | Subscriber | Published-content access |
| 20 | Contributor | Create content and edit owned drafts; cannot publish |
| 30 | Author | Edit and publish owned content |
| 40 | Editor | Manage content across authors |
| 50 | Admin | Site, users, schema and configuration administration |

Audit external authentication `defaultRole`, `roleMapping`, invitations and custom
role checks by numeric value. Older hints mislabeled 30 as Editor and 40 as
Developer. **30 is Author and can publish**; use Contributor 20 when publishing
must remain an editorial responsibility. A UI-hidden button is not authorization.
Verify token scopes and the account role together on REST/MCP requests.

The new `content:edit_own_drafts` permission permits Contributor saves, locks and
taxonomy assignments for owned drafts. Verify own draft creation/update, another
author's draft rejection, publish rejection and published/scheduled edit rejection.
Use fresh revision tokens so concurrency errors cannot masquerade as permission
enforcement. Confirm denied requests did not mutate content or create revisions.

## Revisions and custom ContentEditor hosts

The revision-list REST API and `revision_list` MCP tool include `author` as
`{ id, name }`, or `null` for an unknown/deleted author. Preserve the null case;
do not require user-management access just to show revision attribution.
The standard admin shows historical content read-only with additions/removals,
author labels, a Show changes control and a restore action. Check both the API
metadata and actual editor UI; an API response alone does not verify diff display.

`ContentEditor.onRevisionRestored(item)` may return `void` or `Promise<void>`.
When supplied, the host must refresh the `item` prop to the restored draft before
normal editing resumes. Hosts reading the editor's standard content query already
receive its invalidation. Hosts storing an entry elsewhere should await a reload
and update their own state from the canonical server response. Test success,
rejected refresh and return to editing; do not resolve a callback before that host
has refreshed. A custom field extension alone is not a custom ContentEditor host.

## Plugin MCP tool names

Scoped plugin tools use normalized names: `@acme/calendar` with tool `list_events`
is exposed as `acme__calendar__list_events`. Plain plugin IDs retain their existing
names. Audit saved agent prompts, client tool allowlists, automation calls and
tests against the connected server's actual tool list. Keep plugin identity and
published package IDs intact; only update the externally exposed tool references.
An unreadable plugin tool schema no longer blocks unrelated tools from loading.

## Bylines and guest defaults

Creating a byline from the post editor now opens the full byline form. A new byline
is not a guest unless **Guest byline** is selected; existing bylines do not change.
Check any template branching on `byline.isGuest` against representative new and
existing credits. Custom `onQuickCreateByline`/`onQuickEditByline` callbacks receive
the full form, including `isGuest`; preserve that explicit value when saving.
Do not rewrite existing credits or silently force new bylines to be guests.

## Inline editorial acceptance

On a disposable instance, exercise the real Base layout and registered field
proxies. Check selection toolbar formatting and Turn into, creation of a bare-domain
link with `https://`, caret link preview, edit/remove controls, save/reload and
canonical Portable Text. Empty rich-text fields should mount an editor. The `/image`
picker selects existing library assets; upload new media through the Media Library
first. Verify alt/caption behavior separately when adopting image editing.

## Cloudflare-specific follow-up

Pin `emdash` and `@emdash-cms/cloudflare` to the same version; dev/build warnings
are diagnostics, not version compatibility proof. Root Node/SQLite does not need
the Cloudflare package. On a D1 target evaluate
`d1({ binding: "DB", session: "auto", coalesce: true })` against that adapter's
installed API. Coalescing needs a session and remains experimental; explicitly
await a read before any concurrent write that must not affect it. Measure actual
request/query latency on Workers and preserve schema/backup checks. Local SQLite
tests do not certify D1 batching, read replicas or remote performance.

## Reproduction and receipts

`npm run check:emdash13` is an optional local browser/runtime check. It creates a
fresh disposable project/database, reuses the installed packages, starts its own
loopback server and provisions synthetic users through a test-only authentication
route that exists only in the disposable copy. Real EmDash authorization and
session role resolution remain active. No working database, credentials or uploads
are copied, no email is sent, and no downstream deployment is mutated.

The command writes synthetic API/browser receipts and screenshots to
`audit/emdash-1.3-review-2026-10-18/`. It is not part of automated screenshot CI.
Read the receipt's observed statuses and limitations before treating a feature as
verified. Downstream client source audits are private reports outside Baseline
and the client checkout; they do not certify a live deployment.
